name: arXiv
subcategory: preprint server (physics, mathematics, computer science and five other areas); independent nonprofit since 1 July 2026
origin_detail: Started on 14 Aug 1991 by Paul Ginsparg at Los Alamos National Laboratory as the LANL preprint archive for physics. It moved with Ginsparg to Cornell University in 2001 and was renamed arxiv.org, and Cornell University Library took administrative and financial responsibility in September 2011. A membership funding model began in 2010. arXiv separated from Cornell as an independent nonprofit on 1 July 2026, with Penelope Lewis appointed inaugural CEO and an independent board (announced 30 July 2026).
flagship_projects: arXiv.org preprint server (3M+ articles in eight subject areas)
arXiv API and bulk data access
arXiv-CE technology modernisation and cloud migration (database moved to the cloud on 28 Oct 2026)
openness_notes: Free to read and free to submit. Governance is nonprofit, with Editorial, Institutions and Science advisory councils, and since 2026 an independent board. Papers carry author-chosen licences (public domain, CC BY-SA 4.0, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, publisher or author copyright with distribution rights), and for most papers arXiv holds only a non-exclusive, irrevocable licence to distribute, so not all content is openly licensed for reuse. Code is public on GitHub (e.g. arxiv-browse), although GitHub reports its licence as NOASSERTION. Scored 4 as fully open science infrastructure. Access has narrowed for submitters (endorsement since 2004; 2025-26 CS review-paper restriction, bans and rate limits), but not for readers.

license_history.note: arXiv holds a non-exclusive, irrevocable licence to distribute most papers

risk_events: FY2025 (to 30 Jun 2025): expenses $6.71M against revenue $6.41M, a $297k deficit covered from operating reserves. The FY2026 budget plans $8.85M of expenses and a $465k deficit.
Volume shock: submissions rose from 244,031 (2024) to 284,486 (2025), +16.6%. Sept 2026 set a record of 40,363, double Sept 2024 (20,569), and cs.AI grew more than sixfold in two years.
31 Oct 2025: stopped accepting CS review and position papers not vetted by a journal or conference, citing AI-generated submissions. May 2026: one-year submission bans for unchecked LLM output.
1 Oct 2026: stopgap limit of two submissions per submitter per calendar month. Sept 2026 submissions generated almost 9,000 support tickets.

1 Jul 2026: separated from Cornell, whose in-kind contribution (administration, HR, IT, facilities) was budgeted at $1.89M, or 22% of FY2026 revenue. Our assessment: the new nonprofit must replace that support.
23 Sep 2026: $17.2M in multiyear (three to five year) commitments from Simons Foundation International, XTX Markets and Siegel Family Endowment
robustness: 35 years of operation through two changes of host (LANL to Cornell in 2001, Cornell to independence in 2026). Revenue is diversified: 278 members, whose fees were 56% of FY2025 gifts and member contributions, plus Simons, Schmidt Sciences, NASA and NSF sponsored funding and new multiyear philanthropy. The operation is lean, with 28 staff and a budget under $9M, but it ran deficits in FY2025 and FY2026 and must now cover overheads Cornell used to absorb. Content is mirrored and bulk-downloadable, and its submission rules are tightening under AI-driven volume.
physical_science_relevance: arXiv began as a physics server, and physics was still 30% of 2025 submissions (CS 46%, math 15%). Condensed-matter and materials preprints, including ML-for-materials and self-driving-lab work, often appear there first. For an LPBF alloy lab it is the default free venue for fast, citable dissemination, and its CC licence options let authors make text reusable. Its 2025-26 struggle with AI-generated submissions shows the costs AI imposes on open science infrastructure.
openness_effect_assessment: Free reading and submission made arXiv the default preprint venue for physics, math and CS. It holds 2.9M+ papers, has served 6 billion downloads and reaches 5M+ monthly active users, on a budget of about $6.7M (FY2025) with 28 staff. Openness combined with AI has become a strain: submissions doubled in two years, mostly in CS, forcing quality gates, rate limits and bans that make the server less open to new authors. Independence from Cornell, backed by $17.2M from three philanthropies, aims at a sturdier funding base, but it removes the university's in-kind subsidy.
key_takeaway: arXiv is the long-lived success of open, nonprofit science infrastructure: in 35 years it went from a national-lab physics archive to an independent nonprofit running on a budget under $9M. Its 2025-26 history shows a new risk to openness in the age of AI. Generative tools inflate submission volume faster than moderation can scale, so 'free to submit' now comes with rate limits and quality gates. Its robustness model is diversified support from member libraries, Simons, Schmidt Sciences, NASA, NSF, XTX and Siegel, rather than one patron.
